def transform(grid):
    # Extract the nonzero object, then slant its horizontal top edge into a descending diagonal,
    # while retaining the lower boundary and moving vertical sides to converge.
    pts=[(r,c) for r,row in enumerate(grid) for c,x in enumerate(row) if x]
    color=grid[pts[0][0]][pts[0][1]]
    r0=min(r for r,c in pts); r1=max(r for r,c in pts)
    c0=min(c for r,c in pts); c1=max(c for r,c in pts)
    h=r1-r0+1; w=c1-c0+1
    out=[[0]*len(grid[0]) for _ in grid]
    # identify shape as outline of a roughly rectangular frame, draw lower edge unchanged;
    # top edge is retained on its row, left/right boundaries taper inward/outward diagonally.
    # For each occupied input cell, transform line segments based on observed frame pattern.
    # target pattern: top row keeps its span, subsequent rows have progressively slanted edges.
    for r in range(h):
        if r==0:
            cols=range(c0,c1+1)
        elif r==h-1:
            cols=range(c0,c1+1)
        else:
            # slant left boundary rightward one cell per row, right boundary remains vertical
            # and interior diagonal from split pattern
            cols=[]
        for c in cols: out[r0+r][c]=color
    return out
PY

def transform(grid):
    # Convert the bordered shape into an oblique projection, shifting each row
    # leftwards by the original left margin at the top and gradually less toward bottom.
    pts=[(r,c) for r,row in enumerate(grid) for c,v in enumerate(row) if v]
    color=grid[pts[0][0]][pts[0][1]]
    r0=min(r for r,c in pts); r1=max(r for r,c in pts)
    c0=min(c for r,c in pts); c1=max(c for r,c in pts)
    H=r1-r0
    out=[[0]*len(grid[0]) for _ in grid]
    for r,c in pts:
        # fractional row shear; map lower boundary unchanged, top shifts left by left margin
        shift=round(c0*(r1-r)/H) if H else 0
        nc=c-shift
        if 0<=nc<len(grid[0]): out[r][nc]=color
    return out
